title: irlume machine API, contract version 1
description: One document as written to standard output by an irlume machine-mode command (`--json`). Validating a document proves it is well-formed for contract 1; it says nothing about whether the machine described is healthy. Unknown properties are allowed on purpose: fields may be added within a contract version, so a consumer that rejects them will break on an engine update that is permitted by the contract. See docs/MACHINE-API.md.

contract_version.description: The contract actually in force for this response. Always 1 for this schema.

engine_version.description: The irlume build that answered. Informational: gate on contract_version and capabilities, never on this.

command.description: Which command answered. A new command adds a name here without a contract bump.

code.description: A stable code, never daemon prose. The list may grow; treat an unrecognized code as a non-retryable failure.

retryable.description: Whether an identical request could plausibly succeed later with nothing changed by the caller. Not a promise, and it carries no suggested delay.

capabilities.description: Commands this build implements and can reach. A name is permanent public API once published, and is an availability check rather than a version substitute. The list grows, so match names you know and ignore the rest.

contract_versions.description: The contract range this build speaks. Pick one inside it and pass `--contract N`.

max_profiles.description: How many face profiles one account may hold.

daemon.description: Whether the daemon answered. An unreachable daemon is a reported value, not an error, because the facts that do not need it are still worth having.

auth_method.description: The configured modality. `both` means face and fingerprint are each usable.

enrollment.description: Unknown is not zero: when `known` is false the counts are absent rather than 0, so "we could not find out" cannot be read as "nothing is enrolled".

templates.description: Whether face templates are encrypted at rest. `unknown` when the daemon did not answer.

armed.description: Whether a sealed login password is armed, which is what lets a face login unlock the wallet.

policy.description: The TPM policy the password is sealed against, as text for display. Null when nothing is armed.

key_present.description: Whether a sealed template key currently exists. false with templates=encrypted means the templates cannot currently be opened. If passphrase_set is true, irlume recovery restore can recreate the sealed key from the recovery envelope; otherwise re-enrollment is required. Documented in MACHINE-API.md; added within contract 1 (additive field).

camera.description: Camera capability, never camera identity. Device nodes are not published by any machine command.

fingerprint.description: Whether a fingerprint reader was found.

checks.description: Every readiness check this build runs, complete on every run. A consumer may read an id it knows and cannot find as "this engine version does not run that check" rather than as "it passed".

id.description: Stable check id, public API: the registry grows, but an id is never renamed or reused. The current registry is documented in docs/MACHINE-API.md.

state.description: `unknown` is not `fail`: it means the check could not be carried out. `info` is a fact that is neither good nor bad.

detail.description: English elaboration for a support report. NOT stable and NOT for matching. A consumer that branches on this text has reintroduced the problem this command removes.

display_name.description: User text, not an identifier. It may contain anything the user typed, and it is mutable.

recognizers.description: Per-recognizer scan counts for this profile, and which recognizer the daemon has loaded. A profile can hold templates from several recognizers at once, and only the loaded one's can match, so the flat `scans` list alone cannot say which templates are usable. Absent from an engine that predates per-recognizer reporting.

space.description: The recognizer's embedding space: `embed:` followed by the sha256 of its weights. Opaque; compare for equality, do not parse.

live.description: Whether this is the recognizer the daemon currently has loaded. Exactly one entry can be live, and none is live when the loaded recognizer has no templates in this profile.

known.description: False when no display-manager.service is set: a headless host, or a greeter that registers none. Not the same as "no login manager is installed".

recognized.description: Whether irlume maps this login manager to PAM services. An unrecognized one cannot be targeted by `login enable`.

services.description: The PAM services this login manager consults. Intersect with surface ids to find the entry describing this machine's login screen. A service with no matching surface is one this engine has no wiring recipe for.

surfaces.description: Complete: a service absent from this machine is still listed, with `present` false.

selinux_module.description: `unknown` when the policy store could not be read, which needs root. It is not a synonym for `not-loaded`.

id.description: The PAM service name, e.g. `plasmalogin`, `kde`, `sudo`, `polkit-1`. Stable public API; PAM file paths are not published.

role.description: What the surface is for. The vocabulary may grow.

present.description: Whether the PAM service exists here at all, counting a vendor copy an override would be materialized from.

mode.description: How face fires on a wired surface: `face-first` verifies as soon as the greeter prompts, `on-demand` waits for an empty password submission, `keyring` is the fingerprint keyring-unlock line rather than a face factor, `verify` is the sudo and polkit stanza. Absent, never null, when the surface is not wired.

event.title: Machine event
event.description: One line of an NDJSON event stream, emitted by a streaming capability such as auth-test-events. This is NOT the single-document envelope: a streaming command emits many of these, one per line, and exactly one has terminal true. Validate stream lines against this definition, not against the root.

session_id.description: The exclusive session that produced the stream.

sequence.description: From zero, incrementing by one, no gaps.

terminal.description: True on exactly one line, always the last.

authTestResultData.title: auth.test terminal result
authTestResultData.description: The data of the terminal result event. The match score is deliberately absent: a caller that can read a continuous score can hill-climb a presentation against the threshold.

reason.description: Derived from granted and live, never from daemon prose.

stages.description: The pipeline stages in order. The list may grow within the contract; a consumer must key on `stage`, not on position or count, and must ignore stage names it does not know.

stage.description: Stage name. Stable public API; the set may grow within the contract, so it is deliberately not a closed enum — unknown names must be ignored, and the four current stages are guaranteed present by `modelsListData`.

open.description: Whether this stage accepts third-party models today (#276 opens stages one at a time). `third_party` is present exactly when this is true.

required.description: Whether the daemon refuses to start without this stage's model file.

modelCandidate.description: The model file this CLI process's search order lands on — a candidate, not a claim about the daemon, whose service unit (or an administrator's drop-in) sets its own environment that a shell invocation cannot observe. An authoritative loaded-model report can only come from the daemon.

origin.description: `caller-env`: the calling process's env var chose the path. `shipped`: a packaged or repo location. `built-in`: the stage's implementation is code, not a swappable file. Absent when nothing was found.

observed.description: Whether the search found any filesystem entity for this stage.

readable.description: Whether the candidate opened as a regular file, established the way the daemon's loader establishes it. `observed: true` with `readable: false` (a directory at the path, an unreadable file) means the daemon's load of this candidate would fail.

path.description: Local filesystem path the resolution landed on. Diagnostic; not stable across machines or packagings.

modelEnabled.description: Which catalog entry is enabled, keyed on what the read ESTABLISHED: a value names the model; observed absence (missing file or key — the config directory is world-readable) is `known: true, name: null`; a FAILED read established nothing and is `known: false`, which must not be rendered as disabled.

modelThirdParty.description: Present only on an open stage.

tier.description: `fetched`: irlume downloads the weights from the publisher's origin. `user-supplied`: the license makes obtaining the file the user's business (`irlume models add`). Both tiers are pinned and measured identically.

weights.description: State of the weights file on disk against its catalog pin.
